newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS-BT BUSY AHEAD OF EX-DIVIDEND STATUS.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS-BT BUSY AHEAD OF EX-DIVIDEND STATUS.

text.p: Most of the action in UK stock options on Friday concentrated on British Telecommunications ahead of its shares going ex-dividend on Monday, dealers said.
One of the larger deals was a synthetic short sale against buying BT shares thereby establishing a neutral position.
The synthetic options position involved buying 2,450 August 460 puts at 60p and selling 2,450 August 460 calls at 1p making a net debit of 59p.
After the stock goes ex-dividend, the trader will be entitled to the dividend amount of 46.95p net -- which includes a special dividend amount of 35p.
The long puts may then be exercised in order to sell the shares at 460p each.
Another trader sold 3,500 August 500 calls in BT at 1p.

By 1308 GMT, the shares were up 3p to 419p which was against the general market trend in which the FTSE 100 index plunged 71.0 points to 5,015.8 from profit-taking following a jump the U.S. long bond yield.
The long bond yield went up to 6.57 percent having been around 6.52 percent earlier in the day.
"The bonds have broken through important chart support and caused a fallout in (the UK) stock market," said one dealer. -- Pradip Mishra, London Newsroom +44 171 542 7954
